summary: Staten Island range rear light on Lighthouse Hill: a 1912 octagonal brick tower with a second-order range lens, keepers on the roster 1910 to 1923, a city landmark since 1968.

light.characteristic_note: Current characteristic not verified here; the record gives F W (fixed white, range only). The 1912 Bulletin (PDF p. 19) gives a fixed white light of about 300,000 candlepower when the station was established; the landmark report gives 350,000 candlelight power.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1909 date is the USLHS 'station established' year, when the original second-order range lens was installed. The tower was put into operation and commissioned on 15 April 1912 (Commissioner's reports for FY1915 and FY1916). The record's 1912 is the tower and commissioning date.
The Lighthouse Service Bulletin for 1912 lists the rear light station as completed; the USLHS tower date is 1912.

notes_for_editor: Thin station. (1) The NRHP nomination for 05001340 is not digitised at npgallery (placeholder), so the NRHP listing is not confirmed from a source read here; the record and Wikipedia's infobox give 30 November 2005, which is not cited. (2) The USCG Historian's archived page for this light (Wayback capture) returned only the page header, so it is not used. (3) The 1912 Bulletin entry (PDF p. 19, printed p. 19, page image checked) reads 'Staten Island (Ambrose Channel outer range rear) light station established; fixed white light of about 300,000 candlepower.' An earlier reading of the OCR, 'changed from fixed red to flashing white', came from two entries interleaved in the text and is wrong; the story uses the image wording and sets the Bulletin's 300,000 candlepower against the landmark report's 350,000. (4) Commissioner's reports (FY1915 to FY1922 in the corpus) were searched for the seven keepers in the roster; none turned up, so the keepers rest on the USLHS roster alone and say nothing about their work. (5) No Lighthouse Board report for 1909 to 1911 is in the corpus, so the 1909 establishment (temporary light or range light first shown) is not confirmed. (6) The Wikipedia claim that the original lamp was replaced by an incandescent lamp is not used. (7) Newspaper search 'Ambrose Channel' with 'range' 1909 to 1913 in New York papers returned 34 pages, none of them read for this station. (8) The roster names have not been checked against person pages, so other_stations is not researched. (9) The USLHS record gives 'Keeper's Quarters?: No' with a brick quarters construction entry; the story does not mention quarters. (10) Fiscal-year labels: the Commissioner's FY1915 and FY1916 reports are cited by the fiscal year ended 30 June, so the story's 1912 dates are read from reports covering July 1911 to June 1912 and later.
